title: debt-register template variables
description: Values for templates/debt-register.md.j2 and templates/debt-register.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from debt-register.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

debt_type.title: Debt type
debt_type.description: Which kind this is. deliberate means somebody chose it with a reason - that reason belongs in the record, because it may still hold and the item may not be debt at all.

first_item_id.title: First item id
first_item_id.description: Id of the first entry (TD-001). Ids are permanent - a paid-off item keeps its number and is marked resolved, so the post-mortem that cited it still resolves to something.

first_item_name.title: First item name
first_item_name.description: Short name for that entry, naming the thing and not the feeling - "Order service has no integration tests", never "legacy mess". Someone outside the team has to understand it.

fix_effort.title: Fix effort
fix_effort.description: T-shirt size, estimated by somebody who would actually do the work. An XL is usually three M items nobody has split yet, and it will sit in this register until they are split.

interest_evidence.title: Interest evidence
interest_evidence.description: Evidence that this costs you continuously - the build-time chart, the post-mortem, the PR cycle-time graph. Without it this is a preference, and preferences lose to features every time.

product_name.description: The product or codebase this register covers. One register per codebase - a company-wide debt list is something nobody feels responsible for and everybody cites in planning.

review_date.title: Review date
review_date.description: Date the register was last reviewed, ISO. Registers rot faster than the debt in them, and a stale one becomes the argument for doing nothing about any of it.
